The University of Rhode Island is seeking a dedicated vendor to provide routine and emergency utility maintenance a nd repair services for all underground and above-ground utility systems, excluding electrical, located on the Kingston campus.
The Kingston campus consists of 197 buildings totaling over 4 million square feet with miles of underground utility systems.
These systems include steam, water (potable and non-potable), sewage, storm water and natural gas.
An integral understanding of each o f the university's utility systems is necessary for undertaking the scope of work described in Section 3 of this solicitation.
As such, the selected v endor(s) will be required to study and understand the university's utility systems within the first 6 months of the contract's award date.
The selected vendor(s) will be required to provide pipefitter, steamfitter and p lumbing services, along with all construction equipment, excavation services and materials required to perform the necessary task/repair.
Services s hall also include investigation as necessary to ensure proper repair (locating, camera work, etc).

For clarification, the University will continue to utilize the State Master Price Agreement for general plumbing (MPA #40) and steamfitter work (MPA # 199) for repairs and maintenance outside of the scope of utilities.
SECTION 3: SCOPE OF WORK AND REQUIREMENTS General Scope ofWork Vendors submitting proposals in response to this solicitation must demonstrate that they have the capacity to furnish the labor, materials, and equipment necessary for maintaining and repairing underground and above-ground utility systems, including excavation and restoration services where necessary.
Utility systems covered under this service contract will include steam, potable and non-potable water, natural gas, sewer and storm water infrastructure.
All materials used for maintenance and repairs to utility systems must satisfy code requirements and conform with the University's standards for pipe and fittings.
These standards will be provided to the selected vendor(s) upon award ofthis contract.
Most emergency requests from the University are due to a compromised utility main or service line that directly affects its customers.

As such, vendors must demonstrate they have the capacity to respond to a service call within (1) hour ofthe request for emergency service, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
This requirement includes ensuring the availability ofand providing the equipment necessary for responding to the emergency.
Vendors must demonstrate that they and all response personnel possess appropriate licensure and certifications for performing requested/required tasks.
Evidence ofthese credentials must be submitted as part ofthe proposal.
Vendors must demonstrate that they have access to well-maintained equipment, as well as the resources to provide backup equipment in the event ofa breakdown during an emergency or scheduled repair.
Pertinent utility systems information and service requirements: • Steam system operates at 1 00psi 2017-2 Page 9 of20 Revised I 0/05/2020

o Vendor(s) will provide service up to and including PRVs in each building, as well as associated low-pressure piping beyond the PRY as necessary to ensure a proper repair. o The majority of steam pipe is manufactured by "Thermacore" and is of the jacketed insulated HT406 Type.
Vendors must demonstrate that personnel are certified and have the ability to work on this type of system.
URI has since standardized on a Conduit Pipe-in-Pipe system and accepts products manufactured by Thermacore, Rovanco, and Penna-Pipe. o Maintenance and repair services shall includ e all aspects of the system including main and condensate replacement, steam pit maintenance, steam trap maintenance, drip leg repair, v alve replacement, and welding. • Water system operates at up to I 00psi o V endor(s) will provide service up to and including the building backflow preventer and isolation valves.
Backflow repair certification will be required. o Maintenance and repair services will be required for various types ofpiping.
The majority of pipe is ductile, h owever cast iron, transite a nd plastic exist as well. • Natural gas lines are University owned and op erated.

Distribution pressure is 5 psi. o The University participates in the Operator Qualification Program and requires all contractors to be task certified and adhere to the plan requirements. o This contract will require repair and installation of meters, regulators, service lines and mains, including all restoration services as needed. o Vendor(s) must possess the experience and equipment to service plastic, wrapped steel, bare steel, etc. o Vendor(s) will provide system compliance services including annual l eak detection surveys and cathodic protection maintenance and monitoring. • Sewer Conveyance System o This contract will require service ofall mains and services across the campus to the South Kingstown pump station at Peckham farm. o Maintenance and repair services will be required for various types of piping including clay (VC), cast iron, plastic and transite pipe. o Vendor(s) will provide line clearing, root control, repair, and replacement services. • Storm Water System o Vendor(s) will maintain and repair pipe systems and street drains, providing necessary investigative and drain clearing services as needed.

Calculation ofISBE Participation Rate 1.
ISBE Participation Rate for Non-ISBE Vendors.
The ISBE participation rate for non­ ISBE vendors shall be expressed as a percentage and shall be calculated by dividing the amount ofnon-ISBE vendor's total contract price that will be subcontracted to ISBEs by the non-ISBE vendor's total contract price.

For example, ifthe non-ISBE's total contract price is $100,000.00 and it subcontracts a total of $12,000.00 to [SBEs, the non-ISBE's ISBE participation rate would be 12%. 2.
ISBE Participation Rate for ISBE Vendors.
The ISBE participation rate for ISBE vendors shall be expressed as a percentage and shall be calculated by dividing the amount of the ISBE vendor's total contract price that will be subcontracted to ISBEs and the amount that will be self-performed by the ISBE vendor by the ISBE vendor's total contract price.
For example ifthe ISBE vendor's total contract price is $100,000.00 and it subcontracts a total of $12,000.00 to ISBEs and will perform a total of $8,000.00 of the work itself, the ISBE vendor's ISBE participation rate would be 20%.

Points for ISBE Participation Rate: The vendor with the highest [SBE participation rate shall receive the maximum [SBE participation points.

TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, Finance and Facilities Committee FROM: Marc B. Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: September 11, 2024 SUBJECT: Action Item: FY2026 Total Budget Request Purpose of Submittal: This is a request for the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees to approve the FY2026 Total Budget Request for submission to the State Office of Management and Budget. Recommendation: I recommend that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the FY2026 Total Budget Request for submission to the State Office of Management and Budget. Points to Consider: The FY2026 total budget request for URI is $1.13B. Within this, the FY2026 State General Appropriations request is $146.2M and includes the following components: FY25 Enacted Operating Budget $110.8M Anticipated Operating Shortfall $5.7M Current Service Level $21.6M Strategic Initiatives $13.6M Total $151.7 Anticipated tuition & fee/misc revenue ($5.5M) Total FY26 Budget Request $146.2M The FY2026 General Appropriations includes a $13.6M request for Strategic Initiatives, which includes the following critical operating budget components, in alignment with the Focus URI Strategic Plan: SP1: Broaden Our Impact (Life Sciences Faculty and remaining land-grant state support) $5.3M SP2: Enhance Student Achievement (Academic Advisors) $2.0M SP3: Foster an Inclusive Culture (Support for TD Program, National Guard & Tribal scholarship support) $2.3M SP4: Power the University of the Future (IT Modernization) $4.0M Total $13.6M

As a reminder, last year the Board of Trustees shifted final approval of tuition and fees to the February meeting to make better informed decisions, therefore this budget request assumes a baseline tuition increase of 3.0% and fee increase of 0.7% which will be revisited in February. Finally, the FY2026 URI total budget request includes a significant increase in State RICAP support ($45.2M, 88% over FY2025), as reflected in the Capital Improvement Plan approved by the Board in June 2024. Supporting Information: Please refer to the attached presentation. Proposed Motion of the Board: THAT, the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the University of Rhode Island FY2026 Total Budget Request as set forth in enclosure and as recommended and presented.

TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees FROM: Marc B.
Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: September 11, 2024 SUBJECT: Discussion Item: Approvals Under the Delegation of Authority to the President Relating to Land and Property Purpose of Submittal: This Report satisfies the requirement under the Delegation of Authority to the President to “act in its name and on its behalf, and to execute and deliver all documents and instruments, relating to land and property consistent with the day -to-day management of the University and his responsibility for the general management of the property of the University pursuant to R.I.
General Laws §16-32-2.1.” This delegation requires that all action taken by the President pursuant to this delegation shall be reported to the University of Rhode Island’s Board of Trustees at its next regularly scheduled meeting.

Since the June 28, 2024 Board of Trustees meeting, the transactions listed below were executed under the Delegation of Authority to the President and approved by the Rhode Island State Properties Committee (if such approval was required). 1.
Amendment One to the Facility Use and Real Estate License agreement between the University of Rhode Island and Greenfins Global, LLC to extend the Facility Use Agreement by five months, until October 31, 2024, for continued use of the Fish Building at the Narragansett Bay Campus , an agreement first entered into on May 29, 2014.
Amendment One was executed by Vice President Abby Benson. 2.
An Indenture of Lease Agreement between the Town of Narragansett and the University of Rhode Island at 95 Middlebridge Road, Narragansett for use of buildings and land for the URI Women’s Crew Team for a five-year term with an option to extend for an additional three years.
This agreement serves to continue an existing relationship with the Town of Narragansett for this location that first began in 2015.
The State Properties Committee approved this Lease Agreement on June 25, 2024. 3.

A Lease Agreement between the University of Rhode Island and South County Donuts, Inc for use of space within the Memorial Union, 50 Lower College Road to operate a Dunkin coffee shop.
This agreement continues a relationship that first began in 2013 through an RFP solicitation for a “Coffee Shop” and has continued through June 30, 2024 when a n updated lease agreement was needed.
The new agreement is for a five-year term with an option to extend for an additional five years.
The State Properties Committee approved this Lease Agreement on June 25, 2024. 4.
A Lease Agreement between the University of Rhode Island and the Department of Administration for the use of 17,052 square feet of space on the first and third floors of the Shepard Building located at 80 Washington Street, Providence for a term of three years.
The State Properties Committee approved this Lease Agreement on June 25, 2024.

The University will have a clean audit opinion for the year ending June 30, 2024.
Upon approval by the URI Board of Trustees, the FY 2024 financial statements will be issued.

Please refer to pp. 4-20 of the enclosed financial statements for the University’s Management's Discussion and Analysis, which provides a summary of our FY 2024 statements.
A few highlights are outlined below. x The University’s financial position for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, shows an increase in net position of $45.56 million, compared to an increase of $40.25 million in fiscal year 2023. x When reviewing the University’s condensed statement of revenues, expenses, and changes in net position, it is important to note that nonoperating revenue plays an important role in supporting the operations of the university.
The primary component of nonoperating revenues is State appropriations. x In fiscal year 2024, total operating revenues rose by $18.01 million, representing a 3.57% increase, compared to a 3.96% increase of $19.23 million in fiscal year 2023. x Total operating expenses for the University increased by $27.76 million or 6.0% in fiscal year 2024, compared to a .65% increase of $3.99 million in fiscal year 2023. x The State’s unrestricted appropriation represents the largest component of the University’s nonoperating revenues.
